item.title: Looking for the best typography for equation & formula input
item.description:
Hello Everyone,

I represent a small University Press based on Mexico, we are about to start a textbook series for K-8 and highschool levels so we’re consulting the professionals about the best-suited typography for equations & formula input. The one with all the bells and whistles.
We hope you can help us with some suggestions.

Our considerations so far are:
Freda Serif A
Le Monde Livre
Athelas

Thanks in Advance for your help.
All best.

item.title: Fonts with Prime Marks
item.description:
I’m currently setting something using Electra and have a short passage with prime marks.

I’m wondering if anyone has made a list of serif fonts with decent prime marks?

So far I’ve tried Californian Pro, Palatino, Times… even Sim Hei Regular. Nothing seems to complement Electra.

Any suggestions?

item.title: Greek alphabet + math symbols + sans serif
item.description:
I am working on a redesign for a science magazine/journal and we need a sans serif font with as big a glyph set as possible, including Greeks and quantum symbols and as much math as possible.

Ideally this font would also look amazing as a display face, however I think we all agree that this is basically impossible.

So….what I am looking for is a sans serif with a million bazillion characters that will work well in italic, regular, bold and bold italics (because each of those things means something in science). I am going to try to use it for any sans serif body copy and then insert it in if it needs to be in the display area. It would help me if it had a condensed weight too since I am using one of the more condensed widths of Knockout for the display copy right now and don’t really want to change it if I can help it (I’m rather attached to it actually).
